name: Fairmont Le Chateau Montebello
insider_take: This legendary log castle holds the Guinness World Record as the largest log building on Earth, crafted from 10,000 red cedar logs without a single nail.
whats_special: Built in just four months by 3,500 workers in 1930, this star-shaped château was originally a private club for wealthy industrialists. The property sits on 65,000 acres of pristine wilderness along the Ottawa River, featuring its own marina, championship golf course, and extensive network of hiking trails through old-growth forest.
pro_tip: Book a river-view room during fall foliage season (late September) for spectacular colors, and don't miss the complimentary historical walking tour that reveals secret passages and hidden details about the château's fascinating construction.
dont_miss: The massive stone fireplace in the main lobby that burns continuously, the outdoor hot tub overlooking the Ottawa River, and the property's famous curling rink where you can try Canada's beloved winter sport. Wildlife spotting is exceptional here—watch for black bears, deer, and over 100 bird species right on the grounds.
pros: World's largest log cabin structure with historic charm and architectural significance
Stunning Ottawa River waterfront location with scenic natural surroundings
Extensive recreational facilities including golf course, spa, and outdoor activities
Rich Canadian heritage experience with rustic luxury ambiance
cons: Remote location requires travel planning for dining and entertainment options
Seasonal activities may limit winter recreational offerings
